g.data-info: Central parenchyma cells that store food and water in the young stem.
Bands of parenchyma between the vascular bundles that carry water and food sideways between pith and cortex.
Inner part of each bundle; its vessels carry water and minerals up from the root (protoxylem faces the pith, so it is endarch).
A thin strip of dividing cells between xylem and phloem that later produces secondary growth.
Outer part of each bundle; its sieve tubes carry food made in the leaves.
Layer just inside the endodermis; above each bundle it forms caps of tough sclerenchyma fibres.
Innermost layer of the cortex; its barrel-shaped cells store starch grains.
Loosely packed thin-walled cells of the inner cortex that store food.
A few layers of living cells with corner-thickened walls that give the young stem flexible support.
Single outer layer of tightly packed cells that protects the stem.
Waxy waterproof layer on the outside of the epidermis that reduces water loss.
